answer: The design leans on strict entropy generation requirements tied to verifiable physical clock intervals. Each submission hangs on the garden of a task receipt, and the cipher is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a pragmatic engineering phrasing, concise declarative statements register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the nebula of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
